jetavana.notes: AN 1.1:1.2 names Jeta’s Grove and Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery together. The entry cites SN V 220 when discussing Pubbakoṭṭhaka. SN 48.44 is set at that eastern gate, while SN 48.43 is set in the Añjana Wood at Sāketa.

jotika.notes: SN 55.3:1.3 calls Jotika the sick Dīghāvu’s father. SN 55.2 is a page overlap. The untranslated heading Jotikattheravatthu at Dhp 416:5.0 names an elder, with no indication that he is Dīghāvu’s father.

jotipāla.notes: DN 19:31.6 gives the adviser his title Mahāgovinda. AN 6.54:21.1 calls the teacher Jotipāla Govinda, and AN 7.73 includes him in the same list of teachers who led disciples to the Brahmā world. MN 81:6.2 and 23.4 identify Ghaṭīkāra’s friend. The cited SN 1.48 and 1.49 miss the reunion with the potter in SN 1.50, where the two recall their friendship without using the name Jotipāla.

jāliya.notes: DN 6:15.3, DN 7:1.4 and DN 24:2.4.1 all call Jāliya the wood-bowl ascetic’s pupil. The companion whom the entry calls Maṇḍissa appears as Muṇḍiya in DN 6 and DN 7.

jāṇussoṇī.notes: The packet reports zero mentions. At MN 98:2.2 and MN 27:2.1, jāṇussoṇi exposes both DPD spellings and Sujato writes Jānussoṇi, with dental n. MN 98 lists him among the prominent brahmins and MN 27 identifies him by the white chariot and the conversation with Pilotika. DN 13:2.2 uses the variant jāṇusoṇi. The discourse about extinguishment in this life is AN 3.55. Other page overlaps include MN 3, 26, 97 and 100, SN 12.46 and SN 45.3. DN 19 is cited for a comparison with Govinda’s title.

jīvaka.notes: AN 1.256 names Jīvaka Komārabhacca. Check the entry’s rendering of puggalappasannānaṁ as ‘loved by the people’. The Pali and Sujato describe Jīvaka’s confidence in an individual. The pertinent passages are AN 1.256, AN 6.120–139 and AN 8.26. The adjacent ranges AN 1.258–267 and 1.268–277, AN 6.119 and 6.140, and AN 8.25 are page overlaps. AN 8.30:26.2 names Jīvaka in a chapter summary. The packet misses the untranslated story heading Jīvakapañhavatthu at Dhp 90:0.4.

jīvakambavana.notes: AN 8.26:1.1 locates the grove at Rājagaha. DN 2:1.2 and MN 55:1.2 name the same place in separate words, jīvakassa komārabhaccassa ambavane. Thig 14.1:1.1–2 names the grove as Subhā’s destination.

kajaṅgalā.notes: AN 10.28:1.1 places the Buddha at the town (kajaṅgalāyaṁ). In the very next segment the residents consult the nun Kajaṅgalikā. The candidate describes her, and the packet has no entry for the town. A tap on the town should not present the nun as its definition. MN 152:1.2 uses the place-name variant gajaṅgalāyaṁ. AN 10.27 takes place at Sāvatthī.

kakkarapatta.notes: AN 8.54:1.1–2 names the Koliyan town and Dīghajāṇu. AN 8.53 is set at Vesālī.

kakkaṭa.notes: SN 55.10:1.2 explicitly calls Kakkaṭa a lay follower of Ñātika. The entry’s SN V 138 citation lands in unrelated SN 46 repetitions. In the parallel at DN 16:2.6.6 the Pali reads kukkuṭo and Sujato has Kakkaṭa. The elder in Kakkaṭa 01 is also attested. AN 10.72:1.2 lists him with Cāla and Upacāla, with Pali kukkuṭena and English Kakkaṭa. That spelling accounts for his absence from this name’s mention list. AN 10.71 is a page overlap.

kakudha.notes: SN 2.18 identifies the deity by his questions in the Añjana Wood. SN 2.17 and 2.19 feature Subrahmā and Uttara. AN 5.100 names Mahāmoggallāna’s Koliyan supporter, reborn as a god, who reports Devadatta’s intentions. DPPN has a separate Kakudha 03 for him, absent here. The equation with the visitor in SN 2.18 comes from the commentary. In DN 16:2.6.6 the deceased layman is Kukkuṭa in the Pali and Kakkaṭa in Sujato, corresponding to the variant in Kakudha 01. The packet’s Kakudhā and Kakudhaṁ taps in DN 16 name the river, so assigning the layman to that sutta would misidentify them.

kakusandha.notes: MN 50:9.1–2 identifies the Buddha and his two chief disciples. The Mount Vepulla episode is SN 15.20. SN 15.18 and 15.19 are page overlaps. The packet misses Thag 7.5:4.3, where Kakusandhakoṇāgamano includes both Buddhas and Sujato gives their names one segment later. DN 14:1.12.12–13 names the king of Khemavatī as Khema, while the entry gives Khemaṅkara.

kamboja.notes: Sujato renders the country as Persia. The packet misses the tappable kambojānaṁ in the lists of sixteen countries at AN 3.70:28.3, AN 8.42:3.3, AN 8.43:3.3 and AN 8.45:4.3. MN 93:6.5–6 uses the separate compound yonakambojesu. AN 4.79 is a page overlap with AN 4.80.

kapilavatthu.notes: In MN 53:5.1–2 the Buddha asks Ānanda to continue teaching the Sakyans in the new hall. The entry names Moggallāna. SN 22.80 places the dismissed monks episode at Kapilavatthu, while the noisy arrivals in Ud 3.3 meet the Buddha at Sāvatthī. Clear page overlaps include AN 3.72, 3.124–125, 4.194 and 6.7–9, MN 17, 52 and 121, and SN 22.79, 35.242, 55.38 and 55.46.

kappa.notes: DPD cites both the Thag 10.5 poet and the SN 22 questioner under this sense. DPPN calls their identity probable. The verse attribution and the two conversations each settle which entry describes the passage. In SN 6.4:10.1 the Buddha recalls serving Baka as Kappa. Snp 2.12 and Thag 21.1 concern Vaṅgīsa’s mentor Nigrodhakappa. Snp 5.1, 5.11 and 5.18 concern Bāvari’s pupil Kappa. Neither has a candidate here. SN 18.22 is the Rāhula parallel, SN 22.122–123 are conversations between Sāriputta and Mahākoṭṭhita, and SN 6.5 is a separate encounter with an unnamed brahmā.
